react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this treatment-versus-control comparison. RaMP multi-DB ORA (merged SMPDB/KEGG/Reactome/WikiPathways) returned KEGG:map00150 "Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism" as rank 2 with an extraordinary FDR of 4.97e-18, with 6 of the 8 input metabolites annotated (androst-4-ene-3,17-dione, estrone, 17β-estradiol, DHEA, 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one, and testosterone). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently identified KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) as rank 1 with raw p=5.77e-07, matching the same six metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct activity scoring ranked "Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism" first (p=8.4e-05) with all 14 matched network nodes including six compounds directly from the input list. The cross-paradigm consensus is unambiguous: the treatment perturbs the interconversion network linking the androgen and estrogen biosynthetic axes. Warfarin (C01541) was the sole compound not annotated to any steroid pathway, while 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (C04043) independently scored in mummichog tyrosine metabolism (rank 3, p=0.027), suggesting a secondary perturbation of catecholamine biosynthesis. No InChIKey conflicts were detected across the eight input compounds, confirming the differential metabolites represent eight chemically distinct species and ruling out naming artefacts as the source of the enrichment signal.
